name: Global Wheat Detection 1st Place — Pseudo-Labeled Multi-Detector Fusion
summary: Two-stage object detection pipeline combining Faster R-CNN (ResNeSt-101) and YOLOv5 with heavy mosaic/CutMix augmentation, pseudo-label-based self-training on test data, and weighted box fusion for final bounding box merging.
dejargonized_summary: Detect wheat heads in field images by training two different detection models with aggressive image augmentation, using the models to generate labels on unlabeled test data, retraining on the combined data, and merging the bounding boxes from both models.

outputs.name: bounding_boxes
outputs.constraints: Per-image list of bounding boxes with confidence scores. Each box: [x, y, w, h, confidence].

planning_constraints.subject: augmentation_during_training
planning_constraints.statement: Mosaic and CutMix augmentation must be applied during detector training to improve robustness.
planning_constraints.rationale: Heavy augmentation prevents overfitting to specific field conditions and improves generalization across diverse wheat field domains.

planning_constraints.subject: pseudo_label_after_initial_training
planning_constraints.statement: Pseudo-labeling requires initial trained models before generating labels on test data.
planning_constraints.rationale: The models must be sufficiently accurate before their predictions can be used as training labels.

planning_constraints.subject: wbf_over_nms
planning_constraints.statement: Weighted box fusion should be used instead of standard NMS for multi-model merging.
planning_constraints.rationale: WBF averages overlapping box coordinates weighted by confidence, producing more accurate localizations than NMS which simply suppresses lower-confidence duplicates.

stages.name: Mosaic Augmentation
stages.description: Apply heavy data augmentation including Mosaic (4 images stitched into one), CutMix, and random HSV color shifts using Albumentations. These augmentations increase training diversity and simulate domain shifts.
stages.dejargonized_description: Create more varied training images by stitching four images together, pasting random patches between images, and randomly shifting colors.

inputs.name: wheat_images
inputs.constraints: Original training images with bounding box annotations.

outputs.name: augmented_images
outputs.constraints: Augmented training images with adjusted bounding box annotations.

preconditions: Training images and bounding box annotations are available.
guarantees: Bounding box annotations are correctly transformed alongside image augmentations.
family_notes: Mosaic augmentation was popularized by YOLOv4 and is particularly effective for dense object detection.
CutMix provides regularization by forcing the model to detect partially occluded objects.

stages.name: Heavy Detector
stages.description: Train a 2-stage Faster R-CNN detector with ResNeSt-101 backbone using Detectron2. This model has high accuracy but slower inference. Trained with FPN and multi-scale feature maps.
stages.dejargonized_description: Train a large, accurate detection model that first proposes candidate regions, then classifies and refines each one.

inputs.name: augmented_images
inputs.constraints: Augmented training images with bounding box annotations.

outputs.name: heavy_detections
outputs.constraints: Per-image bounding boxes with confidence scores from Faster R-CNN.

preconditions: Augmented training data is available. Pre-trained ResNeSt backbone weights loaded.
guarantees: Output bounding boxes have associated confidence scores.
family_notes: ResNeSt (Split-Attention Networks) provides stronger feature extraction than standard ResNet.
Faster R-CNN's two-stage design provides high recall for dense object detection.

stages.name: Light Detector
stages.description: Train a 1-stage YOLOv5 detector using the Ultralytics framework. This model is faster and provides complementary predictions with different error characteristics.
stages.dejargonized_description: Train a fast, single-pass detection model that predicts all bounding boxes at once, providing a different perspective from the heavy model.

inputs.name: augmented_images
inputs.constraints: Augmented training images with bounding box annotations.

outputs.name: light_detections
outputs.constraints: Per-image bounding boxes with confidence scores from YOLOv5.

guarantees: Output bounding boxes have associated confidence scores. Inference is faster than 2-stage detector.
family_notes: YOLOv5's anchor-free variant and mosaic augmentation are well-suited for dense small-object detection.
Ensemble diversity comes from architectural differences between 1-stage and 2-stage detectors.

stages.name: Pseudo-Labeling
stages.description: Generate bounding box predictions on the hidden test set using trained models. Filter predictions by high confidence threshold to retain only reliable pseudo-labels.
stages.dejargonized_description: Use the trained models to predict wheat head locations on unlabeled images, keeping only the highly confident predictions as new training labels.

inputs.name: heavy_detections
inputs.constraints: Detections from Faster R-CNN on test images.

inputs.name: light_detections
inputs.constraints: Detections from YOLOv5 on test images.

outputs.name: pseudo_labels
outputs.constraints: High-confidence bounding boxes to use as training labels.

preconditions: Both detector models are trained and can produce predictions on test data.
guarantees: Only high-confidence predictions are retained as pseudo-labels.
family_notes: Pseudo-labeling is a form of semi-supervised learning that leverages unlabeled test data.
Confidence filtering is critical to avoid propagating false positive detections into the training set.

stages.name: Pseudo-Label Retraining
stages.description: Combine original training data with pseudo-labeled test data and fine-tune both detector models. This self-training loop adapts the models to the test domain distribution.
stages.dejargonized_description: Retrain both detection models on the expanded dataset that now includes the auto-labeled test images, allowing the models to adapt to the test conditions.

inputs.name: pseudo_labels
inputs.constraints: Pseudo-labeled test images and bounding boxes.

outputs.name: refined_heavy_detections
outputs.constraints: Improved Faster R-CNN detections after pseudo-label retraining.

outputs.name: refined_light_detections
outputs.constraints: Improved YOLOv5 detections after pseudo-label retraining.

preconditions: Pseudo-labels are available. Original training data is available.
guarantees: Retrained models are adapted to the test domain distribution.
family_notes: This self-training approach bridges the domain gap between training and test wheat field images.
A single round of pseudo-labeling is typically sufficient; multiple rounds risk error amplification.

stages.name: Weighted Box Fusion
stages.description: Merge overlapping bounding boxes from both detector models using Weighted Box Fusion (WBF). WBF averages box coordinates weighted by confidence scores, producing more precise localizations than standard NMS.
stages.dejargonized_description: Combine the bounding boxes from both models by averaging overlapping boxes weighted by their confidence, producing more accurate final boxes than simply picking one.

outputs.name: bounding_boxes
outputs.constraints: Final merged bounding boxes with confidence scores.

preconditions: Detections from both models are available with confidence scores.
guarantees: Overlapping boxes are merged into single averaged boxes. Non-overlapping boxes are preserved.
family_notes: WBF was introduced by Solovyev et al. (2021) and is widely used in detection competitions.
Unlike NMS, WBF uses all overlapping boxes to compute the final position, reducing localization noise.

edges.provenance: Faster R-CNN detections on test images.
Original augmented training data for combined retraining.

audit.rationale: 1st place Kaggle Global Wheat Detection solution. Key innovations include mosaic augmentation, dual-architecture detector ensemble, pseudo-label self-training for domain adaptation, and weighted box fusion.
audit.dejargonized_summary: Detect wheat heads by training two detection models with heavy augmentation, auto-labeling test images, retraining on combined data, and merging predictions from both models.
provenance_notes: Source: Kaggle Global Wheat Detection competition, 1st place solution (2020)
uncertainty_notes: Pseudo-labeling effectiveness depends on initial model quality; poor initial models propagate errors.
WBF IoU threshold is a hyperparameter that affects the trade-off between precision and recall.
